rv.q: So a dreamy production in its look and sound but you do not feel like you have quite entered into its enchantments.
It’s just a bit disjointed, and less of a laugh than it should be.
This A Midsummer Night’s Dream is an enjoyable if uneven affair.
It is an inventive, inclusive and hugely entertaining production that reminds us why Shakespeare's most magical comedy continues to cast its spell.
Whilst some choices feel somewhat clunky within the motion of the play, others are revelations that invigorate the work.

cn.t: This production divides critics with its folk-infused musical approach and imaginative staging. While some praise its vibrant humor and perfect fit for the outdoor venue, others find it lacking a coherent central vision.

ru.inst: £5 standing tickets released Fridays @ 11 AM via Globe's website.
